title: Bilateral MaleCNS T4 optic-flow pathway hypothesis test
question: Does a bilateral right-minus-left visual-motion pathway difference produce opposite-signed steering commands for mirrored yaw-like optic-flow orders?
hypothesis_result: not supported by the minimal T4-only bilateral implementation; not a claim that the full biological binocular circuit is falsified

model_constraints.reason_body_not_run: The pre-body bilateral command did not reverse sign between conditions, so the embodiment gate was not met.

literature_basis.use: Bilateral optic-flow interactions in the lobula-plate system contribute to course control; the study motivates paired-eye yaw-like stimuli but does not justify assigning a canonical sign to the MaleCNS workbook axis.
DNp15/DNHS1 is an HS-linked bilateral optic-flow descending neuron with yaw sensitivity and binocular modulation; DNa02 is identified as a steering-related downstream neuron.

Identified optic-flow descending neurons receive bilateral/contralateral visual information and connect toward motor-relevant circuits, supporting a bilateral DN readout rather than unilateral absolute activity.

stimulus.geometry: Workbook suffix order only; not called clockwise, counterclockwise, front-to-back, or back-to-front.

pathways.selection: Each eye was queried independently from the same 01_07/01_08 workbook suffixes using frozen EXP-002 local stages and corrected T4 -> (visual_projection OR visual_centrifugal OR LPi*) -> descending_neuron selection.

primary_dn.selection_reason: Exact MaleCNS type match with opposite soma side; literature supports DNp15 as HS-linked yaw-sensitive binocular optic-flow output.

secondary_reported_dn.use: Reported separately; not mixed into the primary command because its weighting/sign relative to DNp15 is not established here.

pathways.homology_assessment: The selected DN pairs are genuinely homologous by exact type and opposite somaSide/instance labels. The local T4 populations are not numerically identical across eyes, so the two sides are anatomically corresponding but not byte-symmetric.

readout.primary_command: DNp15_R activity proxy minus DNp15_L activity proxy
readout.controller_mapping: The unchanged EXP-003 SteeringBridge receives only this bilateral difference; no stimulus-direction branch or subtype sign is used.

ablation.operation: Disconnect T4 -> selected lobula-plate/visual target projections on both eyes before descending readout.
ablation.interpretation: The bilateral command is causally dependent on the materialized visual/downstream pathway, but ablation does not rescue direction selectivity.

diagnosis.where_information_collapses: Each eye produces a strong DNp15 transient, but the right-minus-left difference is dominated by a common positive bilateral imbalance. Reversing both temporal orders changes peak timing/amplitude without changing the integrated sign.
diagnosis.likely_scope_of_failure: The minimal model has two independently simulated unilateral T4 paths and a two-hop feed-forward target-to-DN readout. It does not include the cross-hemisphere H2/HS/LPTC electrical and recurrent interactions implicated in binocular yaw processing.
diagnosis.geometry_or_biology_uncertainty: The workbook axis remains unmapped to canonical visual/body direction. The T4-to-DNp15 route is anatomically materialized, but the selected target boundary and dimensionless downstream proxy do not establish the full bilateral HS-H2-DNp15 mechanism.
diagnosis.classification: The bilateral hypothesis is not supported in this minimal T4-only test and remains inconclusive for the full biological binocular circuit.
